title: WiseTech bets on AI, cuts 1700 jobs
full_text:
WiseTech says about 1700 staff have left the company as it turns its focus to artificial intelligence and automates the development of more of its products.
The logistics software titan, which flagged in February that around 2000 staff would be axed, has reported a 79 per cent jump in profits after tax to a record $1.4bn for the year to June 30.
Underlying profit jumped 29 per cent to $243m.
But lay-offs and other costs from its “AI transformation program”, as well as the forced sale of Expedient Software, pushed its net profit down 11 per cent to $178.7m.
WiseTech’s weaker-than-expected outlook rattled investors, who dumped the stock. WiseTech Global chief executive Zubin Appoo – who called in police earlier this year to investigate violent threats an employee had made about the mass lay-offs – said AI had already cut operating costs by $34m a year.
“That adds to the $17m of annualised EBITDA (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation) run rate savings delivered earlier in the year through our focus on high-performance teams and AI,” he said.
“AI has fundamentally changed how we build products, support customers, and work across WiseTech.
“We made more than 500 role reductions globally earlier in FY26 under our high-performance efficiency program, which included impacts from our early adoption of AI.
“We then removed a further approximately 1200 roles globally, mainly in product and development and customer service.
“We did not make these decisions lightly. These changes were needed to build the company we will become.” Mr Appoo said 90 per cent of WiseTech’s code is now AI-assisted, while engineering productivity has surged 45 per cent.
Its AI push comes as the Australian Competition & Consumer Commission (ACCC) raided WiseTech’s office this month as part of an investigation into alleged anti-competitive conduct.
The probe followed WiseTech’s billionaire founder Richard White stepping down as executive chair in July as he faces two live criminal investigations, involving alleged insider trading and claims he exploited a female worker for sex.
He has “unequivocally” denied wrongdoing and is still the company’s chief innovation officer.
WiseTech says it will co-operate with the ACCC’s investigation. The regulator had previously investigated WiseTech over its acquisition of logistics software business Expedient, which it bought when it took over New York-listed e2open for $3.2bn last year.
In January, WiseTech agreed to sell Expedient. It is understood the latest ACCC investigation is unrelated to this sale. Mr Appoo said WiseTech was entering this financial year as a “stronger and more disciplined company”.
